Even though the ideals are distinct if k is uncountable but not inaccessible, it is an open question whether the cardinal invariants given by the combinatorial k-meagre ideal are consistently distinct from those given by the topological k-meagre ideal:

It was observed by Truss and Miller that the cardinal characteristics add(M) and cof(M) can be expressed in terms of the other cardinals of the Cichon diagram.

The same characterisation generalises to the higher Cichoń diagram if we make strong enough assumptions on k. We note that this is not provable for all uncountable k. For example, Brendle [Bre22] showed that <к < cof(M), and thus max {0к, non(Мк)} < cof(MK) is consistent, and holds whenever max {0к, non(Mk)} ≤ K<k.

Theorem 2.7 ([Bre22]). add(M) = min {bк, cov(Mk)} and cof(M) ≥ max {0к, non(Мк)}. Under assumption of kk = k the inequality becomes an equality.

As for the other eight cardinal characteristics of the classical Cichon diagram, they appear to be as independent as is possible in the following sense: any assignment of the cardinalities N1 and N2 to the cardinals of the classical Cichon diagram compatible with both Theorem 2.6 and the arrows in the diagram, is consistent (see [BJ95, Sections 7.5 and 7.6] for each of these cases). This implies that the classical Cichon diagram is complete, as no arrows are missing from the diagram. In fact, Goldstern, Kellner, Mejía, and Shelah [GKMS21; GKS19] showed that all eight cardinal characteristics can have mutually different cardinalities within the same model.
